unmapped_findings: Fe-16%Al monocrystal (Table 1) real composition: Al 16.0 at.% (8.4 wt.-%), impurities C 45, Si 40, O 60 wt.ppm.
The monocrystals contained rare globular AlN inclusions with diameters up to 30 µm, identified by EDX analysis.
No carbides were detected in the Fe-16%Al monocrystal with 45 ppm C after a heat treatment of 14 days at 320°C; without heat treatment no carbides were found in all monocrystals.

In the hardness study (Fig. 1) the as-grown Fe-16%Al monocrystal hardness equals that measured after a 250°C/14 day anneal (maximum ordering), quench from 600°C, furnace cooling from 1100°C to RT, and 300°C/6h and 300°C/3d anneals; lower hardness resulted from 300°C/14d and higher-temperature anneals, and higher hardness from quenching from 1100°C (with and without subsequent anneal).
Short-range ordering was concluded to have no major impact on hardness; only heat treatments at temperatures above 600°C affect the mechanical behaviour of Fe-Al alloys significantly.

The as-grown monocrystal stress-strain curve differs only little from the furnace-cooled and 1100°C FC 600°C Q states, whereas quenching from 1100°C with subsequent 300°C/14d anneal gives a higher yield stress.
